backend.summary: Scanner worker (apps/worker), BullMQ scan-queue + scheduler-queue, GitHub code search client with in-process rate throttle, hardcoded initial ScanRule set (regex + entropy), Finding persistence with DB-level dedup (unique constraint), and GET /api/findings list API. Frontend UI, review-queue actions, flagger, and manual scan-trigger endpoint remain out of scope for this pass (see followUps).

apiContract.auth: requireSession() — any authenticated user, no admin gate (findings are global platform state, same pattern as M02 dashboard.ts).

New reusable apps/web/components/ui/pagination.tsx built (Figma node 7:67) since none existed. Desktop 7-column table and mobile stacked-card layout both implemented per Figma Default/Mobile frames; existing Badge/FindingStatusBadge/Skeleton/EmptyState/ErrorState components reused unmodified. JetBrains Mono (font-mono) applied only to filePath and commitSha; Inter (default) everywhere else.
frontend.actionsColumnDecision: Figma's 'Actions'/'View' column is kept visually present on both desktop table and mobile cards (matches Default/Mobile frames exactly) but rendered as non-interactive, non-navigating text (not an <a>/<Link>) with a disabled cursor and a title tooltip explaining Finding Detail isn't available yet. Chosen over omitting the column entirely so the shipped layout still matches Figma pixel-for-pixel; chosen over a real link because M05 (Finding Detail) does not exist yet and linking to it would 404 in production. Follow-up: swap to a real <Link href={`/findings/${id}`}> once M05 ships.
frontend.designTokenDeviation: Figma frames show literal white (bg-white) fills on the Findings Table, Mobile Header, and Mobile Finding Cards per M04's own knownIssues. Per this task's explicit instruction (and consistent with how M02/M03 frontend already handled this exact class of gap), the frontend implementation uses the project's real semantic Tailwind classes (bg-canvas-default / bg-canvas-subtle) instead of literal white anywhere, so dark theme continues to render correctly. This is a deliberate faithful-in-structure/correct-in-token implementation choice, not a deviation from Figma's visual intent (Figma's own dark-theme variables would resolve to the same non-white value).

Type contract match confirmed (FindingSummary identical across lib/findings.ts and findings-client.tsx). Route wiring traced end-to-end (requireSession -> zod query parse -> listFindings -> Prisma -> JSON). Worker upsertFinding dedup logic confirmed aligned with the unique constraint migration (same field order/name). security.summary: Reviewed raw-secret handling, token decryption lifetime, redaction correctness (full-span masking, fails closed), GET /api/findings authorization (requireSession enforced, no IDOR since Findings are intentionally global/non-user-scoped per PRODUCT_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md), XSS surface (repoFullName/filePath rendered via plain JSX, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML), rate-limiter concurrency safety, and migration additivity. No CRITICAL or HIGH findings.
followUps: LOW: apps/web/app/api/findings/route.ts has no try/catch around listFindings() -- an unhandled Prisma error would fall through to Next's default handler instead of a controlled JSON error response. Pre-existing repo-wide pattern (same gap in /api/tokens), not an M04-specific regression.

LOW: packages/shared/src/redact.ts's edge-showing branch can reveal up to ~67% of a secret at the exact 12-character MIN_MASKED_LENGTH_TO_SHOW_EDGES boundary. Not reachable by any current seeded ScanRule, but a landmine for future admin-editable rules (M08) capturing 12-15 char spans.
LOW: apps/worker/src/scanner.worker.ts has no try/catch around searchCode() -- currently safe (audited call chain never embeds dynamic content in thrown errors), but untested as a hard invariant.

LOW: apps/worker/src/scanner.worker.ts's pickActiveToken() has no locking, so concurrent jobs (worker concurrency: 2) can select the same token in the same tick. Fairness/rate-limit-budget issue only, not a cross-user security issue (shared SearchRateLimiter still caps aggregate request rate).

Migration 20260816140000_add_finding_dedup_constraint has not been applied against a real database in this environment (no DATABASE_URL/Postgres instance available). Run `npm run prisma:migrate --workspace=apps/web` (or `prisma migrate deploy` in production) against a real DB before relying on the unique constraint. If any pre-existing duplicate Finding rows exist in a shared/staging DB, the CREATE UNIQUE INDEX will fail — that must be resolved with explicit approval (do not auto-delete), per CLAUDE.md section 4/5.

GitHub code search 'commitSha' caveat: the Search API's per-item `sha` field is the blob SHA of the matched file at index time, not a git commit SHA — used as Finding.commitSha per the existing single-column schema (no separate blob/commit distinction in the data model). If exact commit-level provenance is later required (e.g. for M05 Finding Detail deep-linking to a specific commit), a follow-up may need to resolve the true commit SHA via an extra GitHub API call per match.

Rule evaluation runs against GitHub Search API 'text_matches' fragments (short highlighted snippets), not full file contents — by design, to avoid downloading/storing full source files. This means some genuine secrets outside the highlighted fragment window could be missed; acceptable tradeoff for M04's scope but worth revisiting if false-negative rate matters later.

ScanRule seed rows (apps/web/prisma/seed.ts) and apps/worker/src/rules/definitions.ts intentionally duplicate the same 6 pattern strings (documented in both files) since apps/worker isn't imported by the Next.js seed script. If a rule pattern is edited in one place without the other, they will drift — M08 (Scan Rule CRUD) should make the DB the sole source of truth and delete the worker's hardcoded INITIAL_SCAN_RULES array once the admin UI exists.

apps/worker/src/token-crypto.ts is a documented copy of apps/web/lib/token-crypto.ts's decrypt() function (not imported directly) because apps/web is a Next.js app not designed for cross-package import from a plain Node worker. If a third module needs this logic, promote both to packages/shared in one coordinated change.
